items.inspect: Record the exit flythrough, and a route that holds the held view, with the native route recorder: T2 engine capture in `fixed` mode, one fresh tick for each submission, at least 1,200 consecutive routed ticks each. Read each take's log first: it lists every routed tick once, in order, at the take's phase. Then judge windows of consecutive ticks, with every tick's submitted image retained, whole and in native-size crops of single movers and their shadows. Judge at least committed ticks 228 to 240 of the flythrough, at the route's phase and at phase 0.9999, where the strip was reproduced; the stretch round its `balloons` checkpoint; and windows of your own choosing across both takes.

items.statement: In Chrome the six stops show the same props and movers as the Mac, with none missing, and along the exit flythrough the movers drift from one tick to the next without popping in or out or jumping.
items.inspect: Capture the six stops and the exit flythrough in Chrome with T2 engine capture in `fixed` mode, every submission of the flythrough retained. Judge the stops whole and in native-size crops beside the Mac's at the same stop. For the flythrough, read each run's source ticks from the capture's records first. A record that repeats a tick, with the next carrying two, is the page deferring a due tick under load: it is noted, and the longer step after it is not counted as a jump. That accounts for how far the scene moves between those frames and for nothing else, so a mover or prop that is missing, new or changed in them is judged like any other. Judge runs of consecutive frames whose ticks advance one at a time, with the stretch round the `balloons` checkpoint among them.

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this work package moved no retained image.

Real-time takes of the build this work package claims are on record as a tripwire, each with a capture-off arm run back to back: the exit flythrough and the held view on the Mac, and the flythrough in Chrome. All six arms ran from one commit with nothing uncommitted. The record gives that commit, each program's hash and one digest of every tracked file there that builds, launches, drives or observes an arm (the files under `crates/`, `examples/v1-game/`, `scripts/` and `.cargo/`, and `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `rust-toolchain.toml`), and for every arm its longest intervals between frames and the machine's load before and after. A capture-on take also keeps its timeline of submissions (elapsed time, committed tick and phase) and says whether it was complete. No interval decides this item. The check fails only when that digest, computed again from the checkout it runs in, differs from the record's, as it does after a change to one capture script and nothing else; on a missing arm, field or load; on an arm whose world stopped before its route or its twenty seconds ended; or on a capture-on take whose median interval is more than twice that of the arm it repeats in `docs/evidence/SHOWCASE/WP5-motion-diagnostics.json` (`elapsed-exit-route`, `elapsed-exit-drift`, `current-chrome`).

At each of the six stops the three rows show the same scene and look alike, each shows what the route gives that stop to show and nothing the route hides there, and each row is unchanged from its own baseline. Every pair of rows agrees under the route check's metric within that stop's cross-row thresholds: 1.0 for the median, and for the 95th percentile and the maximum the values the design's rule set once from the differences measured between the rows at that stop. Under those thresholds the diagnostic scene reaches ten times a threshold at each of its five stops, the exit store drawn with no entities exceeds one at all six, and the retinted texture exceeds one at noon. Each row's stop frames are kept as its baseline, and the row agrees with them within the row's own thresholds. Record: the comparison's run, with every pair's values, the thresholds, each control's ratio and each row's difference from its baseline; the baselines and thresholds it keeps are the launcher's test data.
items.inspect: Run the comparison yourself and look at its submitted stills of the three rows at each of the six stops, side by side at native size, and at a native-size crop of the grid cell where each pair of rows differs most at each stop. Entries 2 to 7 name what each stop must show: a cue missing from all three rows fails, as one missing from a single row does. 1. At every stop the three rows show the same view: the same terrain, horizon and sky, and the same props and balloons in the same places. 2. Sunrise: the sphere and the rock are in the same places on all three rows, and each casts a long shadow across the lookout, of the same direction and length on all three. 3. Noon: the sphere and the rock are in the same places on all three rows, and each has a short shadow on the ground toward the camera on all three. 4. Sunset with the clear Sun, 17.4 h: the Sun's disk is clear above the west ridge on all three rows, in the same place and of the same size. The view is turned 90° from the sphere and the rock, so neither is in the frame. 5. Sunset with the Sun hidden, 17.9 h: on all three rows the west ridge hides the Sun's disk and the sky glows behind the ridge. No row shows the disk. The sphere and the rock are again out of the frame. 6. Twilight: the sphere and the rock are in the same places on all three rows, lit by the sky alone, with the last glow low in the sky. On no row does either cast a shadow from the Sun. 7. Night: on all three rows the ridge line stands against the night sky. No row shows the Sun or a Moon; the scene has no Moon. 8. At every stop sky, ground and props are as bright and of the same colour on each row: no row is visibly lighter, darker or tinted. 9. Anything else one row draws, the others draw in the same place: haze on the far slopes, the sphere's reflection where the sphere is in view, stars at night. 10. Where two rows differ, it is in how an edge, a thin line or a glint is resolved, as when a shipped game's upscaler option is changed, and not in what is drawn or how it is lit.

items.statement: ATTENDED SETUP: at full screen on the built-in display, the exit configuration's Apple recipe row runs the populated exit flythrough in the capture-off release game and holds the display's full refresh in each of two takes. Each take's record gives what the game resolved: the exit's cooked root; a backing extent that is the panel's pixel extent; an output scale that is the full-screen value `APPLE-PRESENTATION` WP17 promoted, which no launch setting forced; a drawable extent that is the backing extent times that scale; and a requested frame rate of the panel's 120 Hz that no launch setting forced. The presented-time witness gives an OS-reported presented interval for every submission from the flythrough's first tick to its last, and the record keeps them all. The witness's own classification judges them: it rounds each interval to whole refresh periods and reports a missed refresh where that is two or more. No interval is a missed refresh, except ones listed with their place on the route, which the record shows to lie outside the game and which do not recur at that place in the other take. An interval the witness counts as one refresh needs no entry, though it is a fraction over the nominal period.
items.ask: Take the two takes one at a time. Is it the exit configuration's Apple recipe row on the exit's cooked root, with capture off and nothing changed but the window? In what the game recorded: is the backing extent the panel's pixel extent, is the output scale the full-screen value `APPLE-PRESENTATION` WP17 promoted, is the drawable extent the backing extent times that scale, is the requested frame rate the panel's 120 Hz, and did no launch setting force the scale or the rate? Does the presented-time witness, as PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC qualified it, cover every submission of the flythrough, and does the record keep every interval? Judge by the witness's classification, not by comparing raw intervals with the nominal period: is every interval the witness reports as a missed refresh listed with its place on the route, evidence that it lay outside the game, and no missed refresh at that place in the other take? Does the record list every full-screen take made in the sitting?

items.statement: ATTENDED SETUP: in a visible Chrome window on the built-in display, the page's frame-callback intervals are recorded over startup and the exit flythrough, with each long interval listed and investigated. The record says this is the page's own clock and not presented time.
items.ask: Was Chrome's window visible and unoccluded on the built-in display for the whole record? Is each long interval listed with a cause that is fixed, proposed to its owning module, or shown to lie outside the page?

items.statement: For each clause of the V1 exit and gate G7, the exit record identifies the evidence at the claimed commit, the rows it covers and the separate implementation, correctness, visual and device status. Its full-screen claim reports the output scale and the backing and drawable extents observed in WP8.6, and describes how that drawable filled the panel.
items.ask: Does each clause cite evidence at the claimed commit for the rows it names, with any iPhone stand-in labelled `proxy:iphone`? Do the GPU culling equality receipts cover both Mac recipes and Chrome on the exit root that commit cooks? For the full-screen claim, do the output scale and both pixel extents match WP8.6's two takes? Below 100% output scale, does the record say the layer enlarged the reconstructed drawable to fill the panel? At 100%, does it say the drawable already matched the panel? Does it distinguish the governor's render scale before reconstruction from the observed output scale?

items.statement: The visual digest shows the six stops on all three rows and frames from the flythrough as contact sheets, small enough to read inside the owner's report.
items.ask: Were the digest's images cut from the captures this review judged, at the claimed commit, and does each name its row and stop?

items.statement: The record lists the physical-device runs owed and every known defect, and the maturity ledger and the README say what V1 delivered and what it did not.
items.ask: Does the list name a physical iPhone, a display other than the built-in panel, a sustained thermal run and hardware that is not Apple's, each with the claim it leaves unqualified? Do the ledger's G7 rows and the README match the record, with nothing claimed for a device that was not run?

items.statement: Every work package the V1 exit rests on is Done in the record files, twelve in all: `PLATFORM-RUNTIME-IOS` WP7, `PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC` WP3, `T2-CAPTURE` WP2, `COOKED-DRAW` WP1, `APPLE-TILE` WP12, `CREATOR` WP3, `APPLE-PRESENTATION` WP11, its paired proof, and WP17, which holds the display's full 120 Hz at full screen on the built-in display, `ATMOSPHERE` WP6, which closes G3s, `BASELINE-GUARD` WP1, `CULLING` WP3 and `CONTENT-LOOP` WP3. `APPLE-PRESENTATION` WP18 and `ATMOSPHERE` WP12 are on the road to the exit and are covered by WP17, which cannot be Done before either. `ATMOSPHERE`'s other later work packages are track 2 and `APPLE-PRESENTATION`'s U1 to U3 are not part of V1, so none of those is among the twelve.
items.check: python3 -c 'import json,sys; L=lambda m,f: json.load(open("docs/plans/"+m+"/"+f)); need=[("PLATFORM-RUNTIME-IOS","WP7"),("PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC","WP3"),("T2-CAPTURE","WP2"),("COOKED-DRAW","WP1"),("APPLE-TILE","WP12"),("CREATOR","WP3"),("APPLE-PRESENTATION","WP11"),("APPLE-PRESENTATION","WP17"),("ATMOSPHERE","WP6"),("BASELINE-GUARD","WP1"),("CULLING","WP3"),("CONTENT-LOOP","WP3")]; ok=lambda m,i: any(x["id"]==i and x.get("status")=="done" for x in L(m,"DONE.json")["work_packages"]) and bool((L(m,"RECORD.json")["work_packages"].get(i) or {}).get("done")); bad=[m+":"+i for m,i in need if not ok(m,i)]; print("not Done:",bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)'

items.statement: Every late frame and long interval that WP7.9 and WP7.10 carried as unresolved under load is answered from the records and takes of the sitting with the other builders paused, at the place on the flythrough or in the day cycle where it occurred: it did not recur there, or it recurred and has a cause that is fixed, proposed to its owning module, or shown to lie outside the game or the page.
items.ask: Take the carried entries one at a time. Does a record or take from the paused sitting cover the place each occurred, on the row it occurred on? Is each answered as not recurring, or with a cause?

items.statement: ATTENDED SETUP: In the capture-off release game on the built-in panel, the exit configuration's portable row runs the full-screen exit flythrough at the same unforced registry output scale and drawable extent as the Apple row in WP8.6. Its record gives the resolved requested frame rate and the cadence achieved, with an OS-reported presented interval for every submission and an investigation of each missed refresh. Both recipes have a windowed startup record through the first exit-scene frame.
items.ask: Compare the portable take with WP8.6's Apple takes on the same panel. Did the portable game resolve WP17's promoted output scale without a launch override, and do its recorded scale and drawable dimensions match the Apple takes? Does the capture-off release record give the resolved requested frame rate and the PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC witness's presented interval for every submission across the exit flythrough? Is every missed refresh listed with a cause fixed, proposed to its owning module, or shown to lie outside the game? Do both recipes' windowed startup records reach the first exit-scene frame?

work_packages.quality_bar: Would pass as a vista in a shipped high-end game: scatter and light as in Red Dead Redemption 2 or Horizon Forbidden West from dawn through night, balloons adrift as over Forza Horizon 5's Mexico, smooth at the display's full refresh. Judged in words from the running game on each row, never against a target image.
